key_insight: ER-Pose replaces the conventional box-driven paradigm with a keypoint-driven representation learning strategy, enabling single-stage real-time pose models to learn spatial relationships among keypoints directly and thus improve accuracy without sacrificing speed.
problem_solved: Single-stage multi-person pose methods often inherit object-detection box-centric constraints that limit keypoint learning, assignment, and multi-scale fusion—this work addresses the resulting accuracy/efficiency trade-offs for real-time systems.
method: Decouple pose learning from bounding-box supervision by designing keypoint-centric representations and targets that emphasize spatial relations among joints.
Integrate the keypoint representation into a YOLO-like single-stage detection backbone with a dedicated keypoint decoding branch and multi-scale feature fusion for real-time inference.
Use tailored training objectives and assignment strategies that prioritize precise keypoint localization and robust multi-person separation in crowded scenes.
impact: Offers a practical route to more accurate and robust real-time multi-person pose estimation while keeping the simplicity and speed of single-stage detectors—useful for mobile/edge deployment, robotics, and live analytics.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: box-driven vs keypoint-driven supervision (showing limitations of boxes and benefits of direct keypoint modeling).
Architecture schematic: backbone + multi-scale fusion + dedicated keypoint head and decoder.
Performance chart: accuracy (mAP/PCK) vs FPS comparing box-driven baseline and ER-Pose.
Qualitative overlays: pose predictions in crowded/occluded scenes to highlight improved joint localization.
paper_title: ER-Pose: Rethinking Keypoint-Driven Representation Learning for Real-Time Human Pose Estimation
paper_authors: Nanjun Li, Pinqi Cheng, Zean Liu, Minghe Tian, Xuanyin Wang
